home.meta.title: react-decor — compile-time @ decorators for React
home.meta.desc: Write @ decorators above React function components and ship pure nested JSX — zero runtime, a fully green toolchain, and lint-enforced composition conventions.
home.hero.headline: Decorators that <hl>compile away</hl>
home.hero.subhead: react-decor gives React function components raw @ decorators — bare, call-form, or JSX — and compiles every one into the nested JSX you would have written by hand. No HOCs, no runtime, nothing extra in the bundle.
home.why.heading: Composition without the pyramid
home.why.intro: Wrappers move out of the tree and onto declarations — what remains is flat, scannable, and enforced by tooling.
home.why.items.zero_runtime.title: Zero runtime
home.why.items.zero_runtime.body: Decorators are erased at build time into plain nested JSX. No library code ships — the output is exactly the hand-written equivalent.
home.why.items.toolchain.title: Toolchain green
home.why.items.toolchain.body: at-tsc, the tsserver plugin, and the ESLint parser all see valid TypeScript — hover, go-to-def, and completions keep working inside decorators.
home.why.items.lint.title: Lint-enforced conventions
home.why.items.lint.body: Eight react-decor rules turn the composition conventions into errors: Slot boundaries, props channels, local atoms, pass-through layers, and more.
home.why.items.readable.title: Readable sections
home.why.items.readable.body: One wrapper per atom, keys at the callsite, zero-prop composition — sections read top-down instead of inside-out.
home.why.source_cta: This grid is compiled from — view its source
home.before.heading: The same section, without the nesting
home.before.intro: A real stats band: every wrapper as a nested element on the left; the identical section authored with react-decor on the right.
home.before.note: The decorated column compiles into exactly the markup of the nested column — the decorators are erased at build time.
home.quickstart.heading: Four files and you're green
home.quickstart.intro: react-decor rides your existing Vite + TypeScript + ESLint setup — one plugin per tool, scoped to *.at.tsx files.
home.quickstart.steps.vite.title: Vite plugin
home.quickstart.steps.vite.body: The transform runs enforce:'pre' and only touches *.at.tsx files. Import it by its bare specifier — the whole chain is plain CommonJS.
home.quickstart.steps.tsconfig.title: tsserver plugin
home.quickstart.steps.tsconfig.body: The editor shows your raw text while the language service type-checks the virtualized code. Select the workspace TypeScript once.
home.quickstart.steps.eslint.title: ESLint helper
home.quickstart.steps.eslint.body: reactDecorEslint() scopes the virtualizing parser and the full rule set to *.at.tsx — while no-key-prop and no-t-prop guard every React file.
home.quickstart.steps.scripts.title: at-tsc + Prettier
home.quickstart.steps.scripts.body: at-tsc wraps the compiler for CLI type-checks, with code frames from your raw text. Prettier can't parse the files — ignore them and hand-format.
home.conventions.heading: The patterns the docs teach
home.conventions.intro: Three load-bearing conventions carry most of the value — each linked to its full treatment in the reference.
home.conventions.items.keyed_tile.title: Keyed tiles
home.conventions.items.keyed_tile.body: Mapped wrappers become module-scope decorated tiles with the key on the map's callsite — stable identity, lint-visible keys.
home.conventions.items.slot.title: The Slot boundary
home.conventions.items.slot.body: asChild wrappers clone their child. Keep that child literal — a decorated atom would send the injected props to the wrong element.
home.conventions.items.enforcement.title: Enforcement
home.conventions.items.enforcement.body: The mechanical half of every convention is an ESLint error, so reviews argue about design — not discipline.
home.cta.heading: Ship the JSX, <hl>skip the pyramid</hl>
home.cta.subhead: Read the full reference — grammar, placements, conventions, toolchain shims, and the complete error catalog.

docs.meta.title: Reference — react-decor
docs.meta.desc: The complete react-decor reference: decorator grammar, the four placements, the keyed-tile convention, the Slot boundary, toolchain shims, lint enforcement, and the AT error catalog.
docs.hero.title: The react-decor reference
docs.hero.intro: Grammar, placements, conventions, toolchain shims, enforcement, and the complete error catalog — with every pattern running live on this page.
docs.toc.heading: On this page
docs.overview.title: Overview
docs.overview.intro: react-decor adds raw @ decorators to React function components and compiles them away into pure nested JSX composition.
docs.overview.p1: No function ever receives or returns a component at runtime — there are no HOCs, no wrapper factories, and no library code in the bundle. What ships is exactly the JSX you would have written by hand; the decorators only exist in your source.
docs.overview.p2: Decorated files use the *.at.tsx filename convention. It scopes every tool — the Vite transform, at-tsc, the tsserver plugin, the ESLint parser, the Prettier exclusion — to a small, visible surface, and everything outside that surface stays plain TypeScript.
docs.forms.title: Three forms
docs.forms.intro: A decorator is a bare reference, a call with one object literal, or a JSX element in parens — each shown with its live result.
docs.forms.bare.title: Bare reference
docs.forms.bare.body: No props. The wrapper receives the decorated target as its only children.
docs.forms.call.title: Call form
docs.forms.call.body: Exactly one object literal, passed as the wrapper's props — and type-checked against them (AT008 and AT009 guard the shape).
docs.forms.jsx.title: JSX form
docs.forms.jsx.body: A full element in parens — the parens are required, since a bare @<Badge /> cannot parse. This is also the only legal form inside a JSX tree.
docs.placements.title: Four placements
docs.placements.intro: The top decorator of a stack is always the outermost wrapper, everywhere. Scoping is exactly what the compiled output implies.
docs.placements.items.decl.title: Top-level declarations
docs.placements.items.decl.body: Function or const arrow, export or export default — the canonical home for static wrappers. Decorator arguments evaluate in module scope.
docs.placements.items.local.title: Local declarations
docs.placements.items.local.body: Grammar-legal but forbidden by default: a local component gets a new identity every render, so React remounts its subtree each time. no-local-atom says hoist it to module scope.
docs.placements.items.return.title: Above a return
docs.placements.items.return.body: Wraps the returned tree with the full function scope available — hooks, props, and locals can all appear in the directive's attributes.
docs.placements.items.tree.title: Inside the tree
docs.placements.items.tree.body: JSX form only, at any depth — and it wraps exactly the next sibling element, nothing else.
docs.scoping.title: Scoping rules
docs.scoping.intro: Two scopes, three invariants, one escape hatch.
docs.scoping.p1: Top-level declaration decorators evaluate in module scope only — there is no props channel into their arguments. Return-position, in-tree, and (forbidden) local placements evaluate inside the function, so hooks and props are available there.
docs.scoping.rule_childless: Wrappers are childless — self-closing or an empty pair; the decorated target becomes their children (AT002).
docs.scoping.rule_capitalized: Wrappers and decorated declarations are capitalized component references (AT003, AT004).
docs.scoping.rule_top: The top decorator of a stack is the outermost wrapper — reading top-down matches the emitted nesting.
docs.scoping.p2: In JSX text, the two-character directive opener would be parsed as syntax — render literal text through an expression instead:
docs.targetslots.title: Target slots — $at
docs.targetslots.intro: By default the decorated target becomes the wrapper's children. The $at sentinel routes it into a named prop instead — and hand-authored elements ride decorator args as ordinary props.
docs.targetslots.items.element.title: Elements as decorator props
docs.targetslots.items.element.body: Call-form arguments accept any expression — including JSX. The wrapper receives the element as a normal prop while the target still threads as children.
docs.targetslots.items.at.title: Route the target into a named prop
docs.targetslots.items.at.body: Import $at from react-decor and write it as a prop value: the transform splices the target element there and emits the wrapper self-closing. Components whose API takes content via element, fallback, or content props become decoratable without adapters — and the slot prop is type-checked, a check the children slot never had.
docs.targetslots.items.compose.title: Render props and stacks
docs.targetslots.items.compose.body: The sentinel composes inside any expression — an arrow makes it a render prop — and stacks flow through it: every directive below a slotted one lands inside that slot. One $at per directive (AT015); never a prop name, shorthand, or spread (AT016); an in-tree slotted wrapper stands alone (AT017). Aliasing is fine — the sentinel resolves from the import binding.
docs.keyedtile.title: The keyed-tile convention
docs.keyedtile.intro: The default for every mapped wrapper: extract the mapped item into a decorated tile, and put the key on the map's callsite — where lint can see it.
docs.keyedtile.p_shape: At section scale this becomes the full-strip shape: module-scope tiles (stable identity), the mapped grid on a decl-@Stagger Body atom, and the section reduced to pure composition. One wrapper per atom with the decl form maximized — a return-position directive carries only what genuinely reads hooks or props, riding the consuming component's own return.
docs.keyedtile.p_forms: All-static attributes take the decl call form. Any attribute that reads props, hooks, or locals — an onClick, a computed to, a t() in an attribute, a className merge — rides the return-position JSX form instead. And when a per-instance decl wrapper is wanted anyway: there is no props channel into decl arguments, so specialize statically — several zero-prop atoms, each pinning its own values.
docs.keyedtile.p_baked: When every usage of a component pairs it with the same wrapper, decorate the component's declaration once and delete the per-callsite directives — the pairing becomes part of the definition.
docs.keyedtile.p_passthrough: And no pass-through atoms: a component that only renders another bare atom is indirection to delete — react-decor/no-passthrough-atom rejects the layer outright.
docs.keyedtile.demo.title: Identity, live
docs.keyedtile.demo.intro: The tiles below are module-scope decorated atoms. Click them to give them local state, then force parent re-renders — the counters survive, because the tiles' identity never changes.
docs.keyedtile.demo.note: Local tile state survives parent re-renders — stable identity is exactly what module-scope tiles buy.
docs.keyedtile.demo.bad_note: Declared locally instead, every parent render would remount the tiles and reset the counters — react-decor/no-local-atom rejects that shape at lint time.
docs.slot.title: The Slot boundary
docs.slot.intro: Radix asChild wrappers clone their child element to inject className, handlers, and aria — so that child must stay a literal element.
docs.slot.p1: A decorated atom compiles to a wrapper around <Name_base {...props} />. Put an asChild wrapper on the declaration and Slot clones the _base element — the injected props land on the label instead of the wrapper. It compiles green and renders broken, which is why no-aschild-decl-decorator exists (proven by a preserved RED fixture in the library's test suite).
docs.slot.p2: The asChild wrapper itself may be a directive — only its direct child must remain literal. One escape exists: an atom that spreads its props onto its root element forwards the injection through, so the innermost decl-position asChild is allowed there (the lint rule detects the spread). Zero-prop atoms keep the return-position pair.
docs.slot.demo_label: A real Button, rendering as a Link — back to the homepage
docs.footguns.title: Footguns, cataloged
docs.footguns.intro: Each of these was hit in a real sketch before the rules existed. The chip names the rule (or config) that rejects the shape now.
docs.footguns.items.key_prop.title: key as a tile prop
docs.footguns.items.key_prop.body: React reserves key: the prop arrives undefined, and dev builds log a console error on access. The map-side key is the only key React uses.
docs.footguns.items.t_prop.title: t as a prop
docs.footguns.items.t_prop.body: i18next context exists so t is never prop-drilled — every atom reads its own via useTranslation().
docs.footguns.items.props_selector.title: Props selectors in decl args
docs.footguns.items.props_selector.body: Decl arguments are module-scope only: a selector like to: ({ to }) => to passes that function itself to the wrapper as the prop value.
docs.footguns.items.static_return.title: Static return directives
docs.footguns.items.static_return.body: A return-position wrapper that reads nothing from function scope belongs on the declaration — scope analysis proves it (asChild pairs are exempt).
docs.footguns.items.local_atom.title: Local atoms
docs.footguns.items.local_atom.body: A decorated declaration inside a function body gets a new identity every render — its whole subtree remounts. Hoist it to module scope and pass what it closed over as props.
docs.footguns.items.jsx_key_disable.body: Banned outright by the repo config: a keyed tile — or a key on the returned element, which the transform hoists onto the emitted wrapper — always removes the need for the disable.
docs.toolchain.title: How the toolchain stays green
docs.toolchain.intro: Raw @ on a function component is invalid TypeScript (TS1206 is checker-level; no compiler flag exists). But TypeScript's parser accepts it — so a same-length, position-preserving swap turns every directive into valid, type-checkable code.
docs.toolchain.p1: Declarations and returns become expression statements: @ becomes ; — or ! for the call form, which type-checks the props object against the component while keeping ReactNode-returning call results out of no-floating-promises. Inside trees, the opener/closer pair becomes an expression container (the sample above shows the exact swap). Because every swap preserves length, positions in diagnostics map 1:1 back to your raw text. Three shims apply exactly that swap:
docs.toolchain.tools.tsc.name: tsc --noEmit
docs.toolchain.tools.tsc.shim: The at-tsc bin — wraps the CompilerHost, recurses solution configs, and prints code frames from your raw text.
docs.toolchain.tools.ide.name: the editor
docs.toolchain.tools.ide.shim: react-decor-ts-plugin in tsconfig plugins — the editor shows raw text while the language service sees virtual code; hover, go-to-def, and completions work inside decorators. Use the workspace TypeScript.
docs.toolchain.tools.eslint.name: ESLint
docs.toolchain.tools.eslint.shim: The react-decor/eslint flat-config helper — a virtualizing parser scoped to *.at.tsx (it also disables no-unused-expressions there).
docs.toolchain.tools.prettier.name: Prettier
docs.toolchain.tools.prettier.shim: No parse is possible — *.at.tsx goes in .prettierignore; long class strings live in formatted composer components instead.
docs.lint.title: Lint enforcement
docs.lint.intro: Eight rules ship with the library. reactDecorEslint() enables the full set on *.at.tsx; the last two are worth applying to every React file, decorated or not.
docs.lint.items.no_aschild_decl_decorato: The Slot boundary at declaration position — an asChild wrapper on a declaration silently misroutes the injected props onto the label.
docs.lint.items.no_props_selector_decl.w: No props channel into decl arguments — a function-valued selector is passed through as the prop itself, never evaluated against props.
docs.lint.items.no_static_return_directi: Scope analysis proves a return-position wrapper reads no props, hooks, or locals — it belongs on a declaration (asChild exempt).
docs.lint.items.no_local_atom.what: Decorated declarations inside function bodies remount their subtree on every parent render — hoist to module scope.
docs.lint.items.no_passthrough_atom.what: An undecorated component that renders one bare atom is indirection to delete.
docs.lint.items.no_stray_at_sentinel.wha: $at outside directive arguments is a real identifier whose runtime value is undefined — it only has meaning where the transform replaces it.
docs.lint.items.no_key_prop.what: key is reserved by React and never arrives as a prop — keys ride the map's callsite element.
docs.lint.items.no_t_prop.what: t is context, not a prop — each atom reads its own useTranslation() (flags TFunction-typed members too).
docs.lint.p_disable: This repo's config additionally bans disabling react/jsx-key outright (eslint-comments/no-restricted-disable), and every other disable comment requires a written reason.
docs.errors.title: Error catalog
docs.errors.intro: Every error carries a precise raw-file span and surfaces identically in the Vite build (code frame), at-tsc, the IDE (squiggle), and ESLint (a fatal parse error at commit time). AT010 is unassigned.
docs.errors.items.AT000: Unrecognized syntax error (a TypeScript parse error passed through).
docs.errors.items.AT001: Malformed inside-tree directive — escape literal directive-opener text with an expression (see Scoping rules).
docs.errors.items.AT002: Wrapper element has children — it must be self-closing or an empty pair.
docs.errors.items.AT003: Wrapper is not a capitalized component reference.
docs.errors.items.AT008: Call form takes exactly one object-literal argument.
docs.errors.items.AT009: Unsupported property form in a call-form object.
docs.errors.items.AT012: Decorator expression is not a component reference, call, or JSX element (no fragments).
docs.errors.items.AT013: Inside-tree target is not a JSX element or an {expression}.
docs.errors.items.AT014: The generated <Name>_base identifier collides with an existing declaration.
docs.errors.items.AT015: More than one $at sentinel in a single directive — the target fills exactly one slot.
docs.errors.items.AT016: $at in an invalid position — never a prop name, a shorthand, or inside a spread.
docs.errors.items.AT017: An inside-tree chain includes a $at slot directive — a slotted wrapper must be its chain's only link.
a11y.statement.title: Accessibility statement
a11y.statement.heading: Accessibility statement
a11y.statement.intro: This documentation site is built to be usable by everyone — keyboard-only navigation, screen-reader landmarks, visible focus, reduced-motion support, and colors drawn from an AA-contrast token palette in both light and dark modes.
a11y.statement.assistive_tech_body: The site is exercised with keyboard-only navigation and automated axe-core scans (WCAG 2.1 A/AA) on every page, in both light and dark themes. Interactive demos remain fully operable without a pointer.
a11y.statement.known_gaps_body: Code samples sit in horizontally scrollable regions; on very narrow screens some long lines require horizontal scrolling. Report anything else you hit — it will be fixed.
a11y.statement.feedback_body: If any part of this site is hard to use with assistive technology, please contact the coordinator above — accessibility issues are treated as defects and prioritized accordingly.
